committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Directly affects the Department of Homeland Security and its internal components.
dimensions.evidence: ensure that each component of the Department of Homeland Security engaged in the detection, deterrence, and seizure of illicit fentanyl

dimensions.assessment: Requires administrative improvements in data sharing and metric development rather than creating new substantive programs or civil liabilities.
dimensions.evidence: collaborate and share relevant information and data relating to the detection, deterrence, and seizure of illicit fentanyl

dimensions.assessment: Does not appropriate new funds or specify fiscal expenditures.
Imposes internal coordination and metric-setting mandates on a single federal department.
dimensions.evidence: establish performance metrics relating to the detection, deterrence, and seizure of illicit fentanyl

dimensions.assessment: Sets a one-year deadline for initial actions, leading to ongoing internal departmental tracking.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act

missing_information: Cost of implementing the data-sharing systems and performance metrics
importance_detail.rationale: The bill directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to ensure information sharing among DHS components engaged in fentanyl detection and deterrence, and to establish performance metrics.
